submitted.rationale: Index 6 (In0.79Sb0.21) had the highest measured EQE, 0.040%. Its XRD shows a crystalline bixbyite-derived phase consistent with In11Sb3O24, which MACE places on the hull and MEGNet predicts has a gap of about 1.9 eV, below the 2.7 eV photon energy. Its neighbours on both sides measured lower.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 0.025%. XRD at nearby index 20 shows mostly substrate/amorphous peaks, and In3Sb5O12 has a gap (~2.77 eV) at or above the photon energy.
Not measured for merit. XRD shows no clear crystalline InSbO4, only substrate-like peaks.

consultations.verdict: Support. MEGNet HSE gap for In11Sb3O24 (1.91 eV) and In2O3 (2.21 eV) is below the 2.7 eV photon energy, so these phases absorb. In3Sb5O12 (2.77 eV) sits at the edge and would absorb weakly. XRD at index 6 shows a crystalline bixbyite-derived phase, while the Sb-rich films look amorphous/substrate-only. So the In-rich crystalline region is the best first probe.

Weak support. Index 6 was very low (0.04%), so I need to probe the Sb-rich side. MACE finds In3Sb5O12 near the hull (0.018 eV/atom) and InSbO4 on the hull, so an In3Sb5O12-type phase could form near index 22. Its MEGNet gap (~2.77 eV) is close to the 2.7 eV photon energy.

Moderate support. EQE is higher on the In-rich side (index 6: 0.040%) than the Sb-rich side (index 22: 0.025%). MACE puts In11Sb3O24 on the hull, and In-rich films form a crystalline bixbyite-derived phase with a sub-2.7 eV gap. The best remaining option is the most In-rich film, index 0.
